profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting at a law school research center between faculty counsel and a contracts administrator to align the legal review and submission package for a symposium-based republication of the political science article, "Unraveling the Central State, but How? Types of Multi-level Governance." The center plans to include the article in an online teaching repository and distribute excerpts in a conference reader for an upcoming comparative-governance workshop. The agenda is to sort out which version of the article is being evaluated, what belongs in the 'submission packet,' what it means for the item to be 'cleared,' and who will actually conduct any permissions outreach if publisher consent is needed. The expected outcome is an apparently shared handoff plan between legal review, permissions activity, and repository intake.

members.name: Elena Park
members.role: Associate General Counsel for Academic Affairs
members.expertise: copyright, educational fair use, scholarly publishing agreements, institutional repository policy
members.background: Elena is an in-house lawyer at the university who previously practiced at a boutique firm representing academic publishers and now advises faculty centers on publication, republication, and permissions questions.
members.private_state: Elena wants to keep the matter low-friction by treating it as a narrow copyright-clearance exercise and avoid creating a broader program-wide review that would slow faculty programming.
hidden_assumptions: When a faculty center asks whether a paper is 'cleared,' they usually mean that legal has completed a rights assessment and identified the permissible path or any licenses still required; it does not automatically mean every operational prerequisite has been satisfied.
The article to be reviewed is the final published APSR version of record because that is the default reference when people invoke the article title without qualification.

A 'submission packet' for legal review normally means the article file, publication citation, and any prior publication agreement or permissions correspondence; ancillary items like metadata, agenda copy, and web blurbs are usually administrative and not something she substantively reviews unless flagged.

If permissions outreach becomes necessary, legal advises on the request language and risk position, but administrative staff typically send the email, track responses, and route any proposed license terms back for review.

members.name: Marcus Bell
members.expertise: speaker agreements, vendor coordination, repository intake forms, conference materials workflow
members.background: Marcus manages operational contracting and permissions intake for the law school's public-law programs and previously worked in university library administration handling course-pack and repository submissions.
members.private_state: Marcus wants a single all-purpose approval he can hand to communications and library staff so they can move without returning for piecemeal legal signoff.
hidden_assumptions: When counsel says something is 'cleared,' that means there is an operational green light for the planned package and no additional rights-related action is needed before posting or distribution unless counsel explicitly says otherwise.
The relevant text is the faculty author's accepted manuscript already sitting in the center's shared drive, because repository intake usually starts from that file rather than the publisher PDF.

A 'submission packet' should include the intake form, proposed metadata, conference agenda, posting language, and distribution details because those materials determine how the library and communications teams will actually use the article.

If permissions outreach is needed, counsel will usually handle it or directly contact publisher counsel, since the outreach may implicate legal interpretation or negotiation rather than simple clerical follow-up.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to getting the article 'cleared' before handing it to communications and the library.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means that she has completed the legal rights assessment and stated the permissible route forward, which may still include caveats or require Marcus to obtain a license before use.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means that the project has a practical green light and no further rights-related action is needed before the repository posting, reader distribution, and associated event uses can proceed.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In university workflows, 'cleared' is common shorthand precisely because it sounds complete. Each party hears the term through their own workstream—legal assessment versus operational go-ahead—so the divergence stays hidden unless someone explicitly asks whether additional action is still required.

misalignment_points.topic: Which article version is under review
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both discuss 'the article' and 'the final version' of "Unraveling the Central State, but How?"
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the published APSR version of record, including journal formatting, pagination, and the acknowledgments page.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the accepted author manuscript in the shared drive, which he treats as the final usable text for repository intake.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both files have the same title and nearly identical substantive content, and in scholarly communications both are often casually called the 'final version.' Because each is routine in its own workflow, neither participant expects the other to be invoking a different document.

misalignment_points.topic: What belongs in the submission packet
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree Marcus will send over 'the submission packet' that afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects a narrow legal-review packet: the article file, publication citation, and any existing permissions or publication-agreement documents. If other administrative materials are attached, she will treat them as context rather than as items requiring substantive legal review.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects a broader operations packet: article file, repository intake sheet, metadata, event agenda, posting language, and reader distribution details, and he assumes counsel's eventual approval of the packet means those materials have effectively been reviewed as part of the same signoff.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Each has a settled internal meaning for 'submission packet,' so the phrase feels procedural rather than substantive. The misalignment persists even after the packet is sent because M1 silently screens out the extra materials as administrative clutter, while M2 later interprets her approval of the packet as approval of the whole package, including metadata and promotional copy.

misalignment_points.topic: Who will handle permissions outreach if consent is needed
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both speak as though any needed publisher permission will simply 'be handled' after Elena reviews the file.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 assumes that if her assessment shows publisher consent is required, Marcus will do the administrative outreach—sending the request, tracking replies, and returning any proposed terms to her for legal review.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 assumes that if consent is required, Elena or her office will handle the outreach because it involves legal interpretation and possible negotiation with the publisher.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase 'we'll handle permissions' masks a common boundary blur between advisory legal work and administrative execution. Since both agree that permissions might become necessary, each comfortably imagines the same next step while assigning the actual outreach to the other side.

When they say they need it cleared, I take that to mean legal identifies the permissible path and flags whether a license is needed, not that every downstream step is complete.
